cards.explanation: The answer is Repent. John the Baptist opens with “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.” (Matthew 3:2) To repent is to turn around, and he wants the people to do it because the kingdom is close. That's his message at the start, and it's a short one. I've seen cookie recipes with more words than that.

The answer is the Lord. The voice in the wilderness calls, “Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.” Matthew says that voice is John, and he's talking about the prophet Isaiah's words. So John isn't clearing a road for himself. He's getting people ready for the Lord.

The answer is True. Matthew says, “His food was locusts and wild honey.” That's what the text gives for John's food. I've served some strange cookie batches in my day, but I have never once put locusts on the tray.

The answer is people from Jerusalem and all Judea and around the Jordan. Matthew says, “People went out to him from Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan.” Jerusalem was the big city, and they still went out to the wilderness. I've had folks skip my bakery over a little rain, so this is impressive.

The answer is True. Matthew says, “Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.” They aren't just getting wet, friends. They're confessing their sins as they're baptized. I think that takes real nerve.

The answer is “You brood of vipers.” John sees the Pharisees and Sadducees coming and calls out, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?” There's no warm-up. I greet my customers with a smile, and he opened with a snake.
The answer is fruit. John says, “Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance.” He's calling for fruit that fits with repentance. That's the word John picks, friends.

The answer is False. John tells the Pharisees and Sadducees, “And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’…” He's not letting them hide behind Abraham, Israel's forefather. It's like claiming you can bake because your grandma's famous cookies exist.

The answer is stones, friends. John says, “For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.” I think that landed hard. If God can do that with rocks, nobody gets to lean on their family name.

The answer is that it is cut down and thrown into the fire. John says, “The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.” He means it, too. Notice it says every tree, with no exceptions.

The answer is False. John says, “…after me will come One more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry.” Even with a whole crowd coming out to him, he says the One after him is greater. That's humble, and I'm taking notes.

The answer is carry His sandals. John says the One coming is “…One more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry.” John says he isn't even worthy of that. I think that tells you how highly he thinks of the One coming.

The answer is the Holy Spirit and fire. John says, “I baptize you with water for repentance, but after me will come One more powerful than I… He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.” Water is what John has, and the One coming has something greater. John says so himself.

The answer is chaff. John says, “His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather His wheat into the barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Wheat goes in the barn. The chaff burns with unquenchable fire.

The answer is baptized. Matthew says, “…Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.” He travels all that way for it. Jesus is the One John was just talking about, so this is a big moment.

The answer is “I need to be baptized by You.” John says, “I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?” I think he's stunned, and honestly, I would be too. A man who just said he isn't worthy to carry the sandals now has this One standing in front of him.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Let it be so now. It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then Matthew says, “Then John permitted Him.” John was hesitating a moment earlier, and now he goes ahead.

The answer is the Spirit of God. Matthew says Jesus “…saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.” John had just said the One coming would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire. Now the Spirit of God rests on Jesus Himself.

The answer is “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” Matthew says a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!” It speaks right after Jesus goes up out of the water. Beloved Son and well pleased are the words that come from heaven.
